title: Emit f_ext init Taichi kernel from lowered Neumann BC
objective: Generate a Taichi kernel that initializes the f_ext field from the per-node contributions produced by the boundary lowering pass.

plan_assets.asset_description: File: codegen/taichi_printer/boundary.py — emit f_ext init kernel

scope: Emit @ti.kernel that writes nodal forces into a global f_ext field
Stay within JIT budget (≤2000 unrolled lines per @ti.kernel)
Mesh indices stay as runtime loops (index partitioning rule)
implementation_steps: Examine existing codegen/taichi_printer structure for kernel emission patterns
Add boundary.py emitter consuming the lowering output
Generate runtime-loop kernel iterating tagged surface nodes
Surface kernel via taichi_printer aggregator so compile_latex can return it
Add codegen unit test asserting golden kernel text
acceptance_criteria: Emitted kernel zeroes f_ext outside the tagged surface and writes traction-derived force on tagged nodes
Generated source respects JIT budget caps (per CLAUDE.md key conventions)
Kernel callable signature stable and documented

cases: Codegen emits expected Taichi source for a single-face Neumann BC
JIT budget probe: line count under per-kernel limit

risks: Mesh indices accidentally unrolled — mitigation: enforce ti.static only for physics indices (range ≤ 6) per .claude/CLAUDE.md

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu' -q

completion_notes: Emitter `emit_neumann_f_ext_kernel(ctx, NeumannKernelSpec) -> str` added to codegen/taichi_printer.py (single-module structure; subpackage layout in plan deferred to avoid scope creep)
NeumannKernelSpec frozen dataclass carries (bc_name, surface_tag, per_node_force) with force pre-distributed (traction * face_area / n_face_nodes) on the Python side
_sanitize_kernel_suffix turns directive BC names into valid Python identifiers; emitted kernel name is init_f_ext_from_neumann_<sanitized>
Index partitioning honoured: mesh indices (i, k) runtime, spatial component (d) ti.static(range(3))

Gate C attempt 1 failed (test_gap: assertions expected '-250.0' literal vs emitted '-250'); resolved by aligning assertions to _fmt_float's trailing-zero stripping with an inline coercion-behaviour comment
